critical_steps: The source inverse is C^{-1}:S_Lambda(R(K))->R(K), so its adjoint maps R(K) back to S_Lambda(R(K)).
For C=S_Lambda|_R, C* equals P_R S_Lambda on S_Lambda(R).
S_Lambda(C^{-1})*K=K is equivalent to S_Lambda^2(R) being contained in R, hence to S_Lambda-invariance of R because S_Lambda is positive.
The explicit frame operator [[2,1],[1,2]] does not preserve span(e1), and the source formula reconstructs e1+(4/5)e2 instead of e1.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact finite-dimensional counterexample plus a general operator-theoretic equivalence for the failed reconstruction identity.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made that invariance alone resolves closedness of every image subspace in the general infinite-dimensional construction.

scientific_limitations: The result refutes the canonical dual theorem as stated and characterizes the source proof's first operator identity.
In infinite dimension, invariance of R(K) does not by itself certify that every proposed image subspace in the source formula is closed.
The related 2020 K-fusion dual theory already uses the projected restricted-adjoint reconstruction; it does not provide this K-g-fusion counterexample.
title: The canonical \(K\)-\(g\)-fusion dual formula fails without \(S_\Lambda\)-invariance of \(R(K)\)
